title: The 4 Best Pull-Up Bars for Garages
h1: The 4 Best Pull-Up Bars for Garages
metaDescription: Our 4 picks for pull-up bars for garages, with key specs, strengths and limitations for each, based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.
lede: We looked at pull-up bars for garages using manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. Each pick lists what it does well and where it falls short, so you can match it to how you'll use it.

products.name: Ultimate Body Press Wall Mount Pull Up Bar
products.blurb: Key specs: Bolts to 16 or 24-inch on-center wall studs, Reversible risers for two mounting depths, Rated well above 300 pounds when properly installed.
strengths: Bolted stud mounting is the sturdiest option in this list, no flex under fast reps or kipping
Reversible risers let you set the bar closer to or further from the wall
10-year warranty reflects genuine confidence in the build quality
limitations: Requires exposed or accessible studs and a drill for permanent installation
Not portable once mounted, a real commitment versus a doorway bar
Installation takes longer than any no-screw doorway option
features: Bolts to 16 or 24-inch on-center wall studs
Reversible risers for two mounting depths
Rated well above 300 pounds when properly installed

products.name: Sunny Health & Fitness Compact Power Tower SF-XF924016
products.blurb: Key specs: Combined pull-up bar, dip station, and push-up handles, 300-pound weight capacity, No drilling or wall mounting required.
strengths: No installation required, just assemble and place on the garage floor
Adds dip and leg raise stations a simple bar can't provide
Can be repositioned or moved if the garage layout changes
limitations: Takes up permanent floor space, a real tradeoff in a garage shared with a car or tools
Frame has more flex under fast kipping pull-ups than a bolted wall mount
Heavier and more involved to assemble than any doorway bar
features: Combined pull-up bar, dip station, and push-up handles
No drilling or wall mounting required
Compact footprint versus full power racks
Captain's chair for hanging leg raises

products.name: Gorilla Gym Gym1 Pull Up Bar Core Unit
products.blurb: Key specs: Telescopic no-assembly doorway mount, 300-pound rated capacity, Compatible with an extender accessory for more positions.
strengths: Telescopic design wedges into a garage's interior-style door frame with no assembly
Extender and rings accessories add options without buying separate equipment
Removes fully when the garage doubles as parking space
limitations: Only useful in garages with a proper interior-style door frame, not all garages have one
Fewer total ratings than the market-leading doorway bars
300-pound rating is lower than the bolted wall mount option
features: Compatible with an extender accessory for more positions
Also supports gymnastic rings as an add-on

products.name: Yes4All Heavy Duty Doorway Pull Up Bar (300 lb)
products.blurb: Key specs: Fits doorways 30 to 38 inches, 300-pound rated capacity, Reinforced steel bar.
strengths: 300-pound rating at a fraction of the cost of a wall-mounted or freestanding setup
Fits the wider door frames common in garage entry doors
Removable in seconds if the space needs to double as a workshop
limitations: Still dependent on having a usable interior-style door frame in the garage
Less rigid under fast reps than a bolted wall mount
Fewer grip positions than dedicated multi-grip bars

howWeChose: Picks are based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. We don't claim our own testing.
We do not list prices or star ratings because they change. Check Amazon for current details.
